text: PERINGATAN: Bawalah bagasi Anda sendiri dari kapal kecuali Anda punya waktu luang 1 jam untuk menunggu. Kru darat tidak bisa diandalkan :(
Pemerintah Indonesia harus meningkatkan fasilitas dan proses imigrasi. Jika jumlah pengunjung lebih banyak pada akhir pekan dan hari libur, pemerintah harus mengambil tindakan.

Ini pertama kalinya saya ke sini... Pertama dan terpenting, pusat terminal ini jauh lebih terorganisir daripada Stulang Berjaya Waterfront, Johor Bharu. Terminal ini lebih mirip bandara dan saya suka suasananya. Bagus sekali Batam... teruskan kerja bagusnya...

Karena pengalaman buruk di Stulang Berjaya Waterfront, saya tidak akan pernah naik feri lagi. Bukan dari Malaysia. Tapi kembali dari Batam melalui terminal ini, itu bisa menjadi salah satu pilihan yang bagus...

Secara keseluruhan, saya bisa datang ke sini lagi...

Pelabuhan terbaik, orang-orang terbaik, pemandangan terbaik!!!

Mantap!!! Ramah juga untuk penyandang disabilitas..dan tentu saja kapal feri terbaik!

Semoga Indonesia & Singapura selalu menyenangkan!

Dini Probojati

Terminal feri yang bagus. Tempatnya tampak agak kuno, tetapi cukup memadai. Loket tiket feri berada di lantai dasar, sangat mudah diakses dari pintu masuk utama. Mereka memiliki beberapa tempat makan dan minimarket di lantai dua. Makanannya cukup enak. Proses imigrasi berjalan sangat baik untuk keberangkatan, meskipun kedatangan lebih lambat karena mereka belum memiliki gerbang otomatis.

Masalahnya adalah transportasi dimonopoli oleh taksi pelabuhan yang sangat mahal, sekitar dua kali lipat dibandingkan dengan aplikasi berbagi tumpangan. Aplikasi berbagi tumpangan tidak akan menjemput Anda di lobi karena monopoli tersebut, Anda harus berjalan keluar ke gerbang jika ingin menggunakan layanan tersebut - yang bisa menjadi masalah jika hujan. Alternatif lainnya adalah menyeberang jembatan penyeberangan ke mal dan menggunakan layanan berbagi tumpangan dari sana.
Area tunggu sangat kecil. Tempat parkir terbatas, sebagian besar tempat parkir diperuntukkan bagi VIP.
Tolong bangun tempat parkir bertingkat atau pindah ke tempat yang lebih besar.
Infrastruktur dibangun dengan sangat baik.
Tempatnya bagus, tapi sopir taksinya buruk. Tidak sopan dan kasar.

KEMUNGKINAN TINDAKAN PENYUAPAN/KORUPSI

Jadi Jumat lalu (21/2/2025), kami bertiga (ibu, saudara laki-laki, dan saya) sedang berlibur akhir pekan ke Batam.

Kami tiba di Terminal Feri Batam Center pukul 9 pagi waktu setempat. Saat mengantre untuk pemeriksaan paspor, saya sedang mengatur roaming untuk mengisi Visa of Arrival (VOA). Di sana, saya dipanggil oleh seorang petugas imigrasi ke kantornya dan ponsel ibu saya dan saya, bersama dengan paspor saya, diambil oleh petugas imigrasi tersebut. Kemudian, dia menyuruh saya menunggu di luar kantornya (saat itu pukul 9.30 pagi waktu Batam). Kira-kira setelah 20-30 menit, dia keluar dari ruang kantornya untuk melayani petugas lain, tetapi ketika dia melihat saya, dia bertanya "kamu ngapain di sini?" dua kali karena saya benar-benar tidak tahu apa-apa. Kemudian saya mengatakan kepadanya bahwa ponsel dan paspor saya diambil olehnya. Dia kemudian dengan kasar berkata kepada saya "ha tahu pun kamu, kamu tahu tidak apa salahmu?" Saya menjawab, “Saya tadi sedang mengatur layanan roaming saya untuk mengisi VOA saya”. Kemudian, dia memberi tahu saya bahwa roaming dapat dilakukan setelah imigrasi di luar. Saya kemudian hanya diam dan mengangguk pelan. Dia kemudian kembali ke ruangannya dan menghilang entah berapa jam. Sambil menunggu tindakannya, saya hanya duduk di kursi, tidak memprovokasi atau meminta pembebasan karena saya percaya dia hanya melakukan pekerjaannya. Kemudian, ada seorang pria duduk tepat di sebelah saya bertanya apa yang terjadi. Saya mengatakan kepadanya bahwa paspor dan ponsel saya diambil oleh petugas. Dia kemudian dengan lembut mengatakan bahwa dia dapat menawarkan bantuan. Karena curiga dengan tawaran itu (saya merasa bahwa bantuannya disertai dengan uang tip/uang sampingan, saya menjawabnya “Tidak, Papa. Aku tunggu saja”). Pria itu kemudian meninggalkan saya dan pergi menemui pelanggar lain (tidak secara langsung tetapi secara berkala dia akan masuk ke ruangan).

Perlu diingat bahwa selama saya menunggu, ada banyak pelanggar setelah saya yang dibebaskan dalam waktu kurang dari 10 menit menunggu (salah satunya langsung bersama pria yang menawarkan bantuan kepada saya).

Singkat cerita, saya ditahan di ruang tunggu, dari jam 9 pagi sampai 1.30 siang. Saat hendak dibebaskan, petugas wanita itu menyuruh saya untuk tidak menggunakan telepon lagi sambil menunggu pemeriksaan imigrasi. Karena frustrasi ditahan begitu lama tanpa telepon dan paspor, saya menjawabnya dengan satu kata, "mungkin". Dia marah dan langsung menolak masuk saya. Saya bilang padanya, "Tidak apa-apa. Kirim saja saya kembali ke Malaysia karena saya sudah lelah secara mental dan fisik karena menunggu."

Sambil menunggu feri kembali, dia datang kepada saya dan meminta saya untuk menelepon keluarga saya. Rupanya, ketika petugas feri memberi tahu ibu saya bahwa saya akan dipulangkan karena perilaku "tidak sopan", ibu saya menanyakan nama petugas wanita itu kepada petugas feri, dan ingin melaporkannya karena tuduhan yang salah. Saya dituduh bermain ponsel meskipun sudah dua kali diperingatkan oleh petugas lain (padahal, saya sama sekali tidak diperingatkan atas pelanggaran tersebut). Kemudian dia mengizinkan saya masuk setelah mendengar bahwa ibu saya ingin melaporkannya atas kemungkinan tindakan korupsi dan salah tafsir (karena pukul 11.30 pagi waktu Batam, ibu saya masuk ke ruang tunggu untuk menemui saya, dan saya mengatakan kepadanya bahwa ada seorang pria lokal yang menawarkan bantuan kepada saya). Foto terakhir adalah pria yang menawarkan bantuan kepada saya, sedang berbincang dengan petugas wanita tersebut.

Postingan ini bukan untuk menuduh petugas tersebut melakukan tindakan korupsi, tetapi agar pengunjung lebih waspada terhadap kejadian "pemeriksaan acak/penggunaan ponsel saat di imigrasi" yang sering terjadi. Juga, agar pihak berwenang menyelidiki keberadaan pria yang menawarkan bantuan kepada saya di kantor Imigrasi Batam Center Ferry. Mengapa dia berada di kantor hampir sepanjang waktu? Juga kepada Ibu Cia, Anda telah membuat saya menunggu selama 4 jam seperti orang bodoh, dan Anda tidak pantas mendapatkan rasa hormat saya.

Singkatnya - PANAS. HARGA/TAKSI PENIPUAN. Tidak higienis.
Tempat ini sangat panas. Saya makan siang di sini, dan sayangnya, panasnya membuat saya kehilangan kesabaran. Pintu masuknya, yang dekat dengan kamar mandi, sangat bau dan tidak nyaman saat saya menunggu untuk masuk.
😖😖😖😖 Mengapa harga di dalam tempat ini sangat mahal?

Di luar, semua sopir taksi terus memaksa kami untuk naik taksi mereka, dan mengenakan biaya 100 ribu untuk perjalanan 3 km terasa seperti penipuan. Salut untuk sopir penipu ini—saya sudah menyimpan nomor kontaknya.
Selamat menikmati!

Pelabuhan yang kompak dan efisien ini, menurut saya, PERLU direnovasi karena terasa sangat tua dan ketinggalan zaman. Meskipun begitu, pelabuhan ini berfungsi dengan baik, tidak ada kemacetan atau hambatan, tetapi akan lebih baik jika direnovasi dan ditambahkan jalur untuk imigrasi dan mungkin dipasang gerbang otomatis.

Terminal feri yang berantakan. Ohh, tolonglah. Bongkar dan bangun kembali yang baru dengan standar internasional. Para pelancong harap berhati-hati karena tidak ada lift dan naik dengan bagasi berat serta turun menggunakan tangga. Eskalator turun rusak. Loket check-in bagasi sangat menantang. Harap antre lebih awal karena antrean bisa menjadi berantakan dan terlalu panjang. Secara keseluruhan, terminal feri ini membutuhkan banyak perbaikan. Lain kali saya akan menggunakan Harbour Bay saja.
Bagus sekali
Transit cepat keluar dari terminal
Tempat yang bagus
Tempat yang bagus untuk transisi.

Di dalam feri lumayan, ada KFC (dengan wifi), tempat penukaran uang, dan agen feri.
Namun, begitu Anda keluar, perbedaannya sangat besar.
Hal pertama yang akan Anda alami adalah jalan setapak yang belum selesai dan tertutup rumput.
Jika Anda berkunjung setelah hujan, jalan berlumpur akan membuat Anda menangis.
Namun, staf bea cukai cukup ramah, sabar, dan membantu, dan hanya butuh sekitar 15 menit untuk menyelesaikan semuanya, lebih cepat jika Anda bebas visa.
Masalah keterlambatan feri...

PETUGAS IMIGRASI KORUP DI TERMINAL FERI INI

Pada tanggal 21 Februari, saya dan keluarga berencana mengunjungi Batam, Indonesia. Liburan Tahun Baru Imlek baru saja berlalu, dan kami menginginkan liburan singkat dan tenang—dua hari istirahat dan jalan-jalan sebelum ibu saya kembali ke Filipina. Rencananya hanya untuk waktu keluarga yang sederhana.

Kami pemegang paspor Filipina - suami, saya, dan putri saya memiliki izin tinggal jangka panjang Singapura yang masih berlaku. Pemerintah Indonesia memberikan izin masuk bebas visa 30 hari bagi pemegang paspor Filipina. Kami memiliki tiket pulang pergi dalam jangka waktu yang diizinkan. Kami sudah memesan hotel. Semuanya berjalan lancar.

Namun, saat kami tiba di imigrasi Batam pada tanggal 21 Februari 2026, pukul 10.30 pagi waktu Indonesia, semuanya berubah.

Tiba-tiba kami ditahan dan diinterogasi. Petugas menuduh kami melakukan perjalanan ke Batam "hanya untuk memperpanjang visa ibu saya di Singapura." Tuduhan ini mengejutkan kami. Mengapa imigrasi Indonesia harus khawatir tentang kebijakan ICA Singapura? Kami memasuki Indonesia secara legal berdasarkan skema bebas visa Indonesia. Kami tidak tinggal melebihi batas waktu di mana pun. Kami tidak melanggar hukum Indonesia apa pun.

Meskipun menjelaskan bahwa ini adalah perjalanan liburan singkat 2 hari, kami diantar ke sebuah kantor untuk "interogasi" lebih lanjut.

Ruangan itu remang-remang dan tegang. Ada turis lain di dalam juga, termasuk pemegang paspor India yang juga tampak gelisah. Suasana terasa mengintimidasi. Pertanyaan diulang-ulang. Nada bicaranya menuduh, seolah-olah kami telah melakukan kesalahan.

Kemudian nada bicara petugas berubah.

Dia memberi tahu kami bahwa kami memiliki "dua pilihan":
1. Mengubah penerbangan ibu saya dan memesankan tiket kembali ke Filipina pada tanggal yang mereka inginkan.

2. Membayar SGD 150 sebagai "denda" karena "transit" di Batam.

Denda untuk pelanggaran apa? Tidak ada penjelasan yang jelas. Tidak ada pemberitahuan tertulis. Tidak ada tanda terima resmi yang disebutkan di muka. Tidak ada dakwaan resmi. Hanya dua "pilihan."

Mengapa imigrasi Indonesia harus menentukan kapan ibu saya terbang kembali ke Filipina? Mengapa ada "denda" padahal kami masih berada dalam aturan bebas visa Indonesia?

Saat itu, rasa takut menguasai kami. Kami berada di kantor imigrasi asing. Kami melihat bagaimana petugas berbicara kepada turis lain. Kami tidak tahu apa yang akan terjadi selanjutnya—apakah mereka akan menolak masuk? Membatalkan paspor kami? Memasukkan kami ke daftar hitam? Membuat komplikasi lebih lanjut untuk perjalanan kami?

Merasa terintimidasi dan tidak berdaya, dan ingin menghindari masalah lebih lanjut, kami setuju untuk membayar uang tersebut.

Apa yang seharusnya menjadi perjalanan keluarga yang santai berubah menjadi pengalaman yang sangat menegangkan dan meresahkan. Hal ini membuat para pelancong mempertanyakan:
1. Apakah perjalanan liburan singkat sekarang mencurigakan?

2. Apakah mengunjungi Batam setelah tinggal di Singapura secara otomatis dianggap sebagai pelanggaran?

3. Mengapa turis ditekan dengan "denda" yang tidak jelas tanpa pelanggaran tertulis yang jelas?

Pengalaman seperti ini merusak kepercayaan. Pariwisata berkembang berdasarkan keselamatan, keadilan, dan transparansi. Ketika para pelancong merasa terintimidasi atau ditekan tanpa dasar hukum yang jelas, hal itu menciptakan rasa takut—bukan kepercayaan diri.

Kami datang untuk beristirahat dan berwisata. Kami pergi dengan kekecewaan.

Ini kemungkinan akan menjadi kunjungan terakhir kami ke Batam.

Kepada sesama pelancong: selalu siapkan dokumen lengkap, pahami aturan visa Anda, dan tetap tenang—tetapi juga sadari hak-hak Anda. Liburan tidak seharusnya dimulai dengan rasa takut.

KORUPSI!

Insiden ini benar-benar meninggalkan trauma pada pengalaman saya saat berkunjung ke Batam.

Saya dan pasangan saya 'ditahan' di sebuah ruangan bersama banyak orang lain dari berbagai negara (SG, MY, PH, BD, CN, dll.), masing-masing dengan masalah kecil/tidak serius yang berbeda, dan tidak satu pun dari kami diberi tahu alasan penahanan kami selama setidaknya satu jam. Mereka mengambil paspor kami dan meletakkannya di ruangan kosong. Setelah menunggu lebih dari satu jam, petugas akhirnya memanggil kami ke ruangan, satu per satu. Mereka mulai berteriak, "APAKAH KALIAN TAHU KESALAHAN KALIAN?!, ITU SANGAT TIDAK SOPAN!" Tentu saja, awalnya tidak ada dari kami yang tahu apa kesalahan kami, sampai mereka memberikan alasan (yang bisa apa saja). Setelah berteriak dan berusaha sekuat tenaga untuk menanamkan rasa takut, sambil merokok dan menggunakan vape secara bersamaan, mereka memberi kami 2 pilihan:
1. Kembali ke Singapura dengan feri berikutnya (yang merupakan hari berikutnya karena tidak ada feri lagi malam itu)
2. Membayar denda sebesar 100 SGD masing-masing.

Para petugas tidak akan pernah membiarkan kami pergi tanpa membayar, dan saya mulai melihat banyak orang lain membayar saat mereka ditahan selama berjam-jam. Akhirnya kami menyerah dan membayar 'denda' tersebut, setelah 2 jam. Saat itulah kami melihat setumpuk uang tunai di bawah keyboard di ruang interogasi mereka.

Pengalaman yang sangat menakutkan dan tindakan korupsi yang terang-terangan. Semua petugas bersekongkol, dan tampaknya itu adalah hal yang biasa bagi mereka semua.
Tunggu COVID dan nanti akan dibuka.

Peringatan Korupsi di Bea Cukai Terminal Feri Batam Centre (13 Maret 2026)

Tiba di Batam Centre melalui feri malam dari HarbourFront dan mengalami pemerasan terang-terangan oleh petugas bea cukai.

Saat mengantre untuk pemeriksaan paspor, kami pindah ke antrean autogate yang lebih pendek. Seorang petugas menghentikan kami dan mengantar kami ke "ruang interogasi" tersembunyi yang tidak terlihat oleh publik. Di dalam, beberapa warga asing sudah menunggu.

Satu per satu, kami dipanggil masuk. Seorang pelancong Filipina sebelum kami dipaksa membayar "denda" atas kondisi paspornya.

Ketika giliran kami, pasangan saya keluar dan berkata: "Mereka menginginkan uang."

Di dalam ruang interogasi, saya dituduh oleh dua petugas melakukan "pelanggaran tidak sopan" karena diduga melewati pembatas. Para petugas berteriak, menyita ponsel saya, mengintimidasi, dan menuntut denda SGD 100 per orang.

Saya diancam dengan dua pilihan: membayar segera atau ditahan semalaman dan dipaksa kembali ke Singapura keesokan harinya.

Setelah 1,5 jam intimidasi, ancaman, dan tekanan yang tidak beralasan, kami membayar denda meskipun tidak melakukan kesalahan apa pun.

Ini bukan penegakan hukum. Ini adalah paksaan dan pemerasan yang menargetkan para pelancong.

Saya akan mempertimbangkan kembali untuk kembali ke Batam.

Kepada semua pelancong, perlu diingat bahwa berhati-hati mungkin tidak membantu karena Anda bisa dipaksa membayar denda dengan alasan apa pun. Mungkin berdoa untuk keberuntungan yang lebih baik atau menghindari Batam dengan segala cara akan menjadi pilihan yang lebih baik. Tetap aman dan semoga beruntung.

Pengalaman yang benar-benar mengerikan dan korup di imigrasi saat tiba dari Terminal HarbourFront ke Batam Centre. Terjadi pada 14 Februari 2026, sekitar pukul 13.00 - 15.30.

Saya ditahan karena paspor yang disebut "rusak" padahal saya baru saja melakukan perjalanan internasional tanpa masalah sama sekali. Ketika saya mencoba menjelaskan, petugas itu bersikap kasar dan meremehkan, mengatakan "Ini Indonesia, bukan Thailand" alih-alih memberikan alasan atau solusi yang tepat.

Kemudian bagian yang paling mengejutkan terjadi. Saya diberitahu bahwa petugas imigrasi "tidak dapat membantu" dan didorong untuk berbicara dengan seorang "agen" yang menawarkan tiga pilihan kepada saya:
• Kembali ke Singapura
• Menunggu berjam-jam sampai mereka merasa puas (mungkin sampai shift malam)
• Membayar "biaya" untuk menyelesaikannya

Sangat jelas mereka menekan saya untuk membayar uang. Ini terasa seperti penyuapan dan penyalahgunaan kekuasaan, bukan proses imigrasi yang sah. SAYA DIRAMPAS SEBESAR IDR 500.000.

Saya datang ke Batam untuk kegiatan amal membantu panti asuhan dan orang-orang yang membutuhkan, tetapi malah diperlakukan seperti target untuk diperas uangnya. Benar-benar tidak etis, membuat stres, dan memalukan.

Pengalaman ini saja membuat saya tidak ingin menginjakkan kaki di Batam lagi.
Wisatawan harus sangat berhati-hati. Ini bukan cara kerja imigrasi yang seharusnya. Selain itu, tolong sembunyikan uang tunai Anda. Mereka akan memeriksa isi tas Anda untuk melihat berapa banyak uang yang Anda bawa.
Sudah pernah ke sini sekali

Pelayanan dan fasilitas buruk. Tidak ada lift. Troli untuk bagasi ada, tetapi entah mengapa tidak tersedia untuk umum. Sudah bertanya di meja informasi tetapi stafnya tidak membantu. Struktur keseluruhan tempat ini tidak ramah bagi penyandang disabilitas. Tidak direkomendasikan.
Ramai pengunjung, tidak akan bosan saat menunggu, ada toko suvenir dan ruang sholat.

Terbaik

Hei, para pejabat pemerintah. Jika Anda ingin orang-orang berhenti menganggap negara Anda sebagai negara terbelakang dunia ketiga, mungkin berhentilah menerima suap dan mulailah merawat fasilitas Anda. Belum sampai 10 langkah setelah memasuki Indonesia, saya dikerumuni orang-orang yang menawarkan tumpangan taksi dengan harga selangit, bahkan ada yang terus mengganggu saya ketika saya menyeberang jalan untuk bertemu dengan penumpang tumpangan saya!

Mengapa saya menyeberang jalan, mungkin Anda bertanya? Karena percaya atau tidak, para pengemudi taksi bersekongkol dan melarang semua tumpangan untuk menjemput penumpang di dalam fasilitas pelabuhan. Ya, ini tahun 2024 dan begitulah cara orang Indonesia masih bertindak. Saya tidak akan heran jika para pejabat menerima suap yang besar dari para pengemudi taksi ini dan terus menutup mata terhadap hal ini.

Anda semua harus ingat bahwa ini adalah pelabuhan masuk, tempat banyak orang mendapatkan kesan pertama mereka tentang Indonesia untuk pertama kalinya. Dan sebagai negara yang suka menampilkan citra yang baik, mereka masih sangat buruk dalam mengelola hal ini. Saya bahkan tidak bisa membayangkan betapa mengerikan kondisi kehidupan masyarakat Indonesia yang tinggal jauh dari tempat wisata. Ini memalukan bagi bangsa Anda.

Nah, seperti yang sudah diketahui oleh seluruh dunia, staf pemerintah Indonesia memiliki beberapa masalah dalam melayani masyarakat. Jadi, mari kita bersyukur atas 'manajemen perubahan' yang lambat ini. Setidaknya mereka berubah :D

Saya memberi nilai rendah bukan karena arsitekturnya, tetapi karena petugas imigrasi di sana. Mereka seperti perampok. Sekupang Ferry Terminal is one of the main ports in Batam City, serving domestic and international sea transportation. Located in the Sekupang area, the port is divided into two sections: the domestic terminal and the international terminal. The domestic terminal serves inter-island routes to Karimun, Tanjung Balai, Dumai, and other islands in the Riau region, while the international terminal serves fast routes to Singapore and Malaysia, with a travel time of approximately 45 minutes.

The facilities at Sekupang Ferry Terminal are comprehensive and modern. It features air-conditioned waiting rooms, well-organized ticket counters, a dining area and cafe, money changers, ATMs, and a prayer room. Land transportation services such as official taxis and ample parking are also available. The international terminal even features a business lounge, free Wi-Fi, and a fast and efficient immigration system, making it a popular alternative for passengers looking to avoid the crowds at Batam Center Port.

Beyond its primary function as a passenger port, Sekupang Ferry Terminal also serves as a focal point for Batam for international tourists. With its modern, clean appearance and increasingly professional service, this terminal plays a vital role in supporting the tourism sector and public mobility. Its strategic location near residential areas such as Tiban, Batu Aji, and Tanjung Riau also makes it a preferred port for both locals and travelers.

This happened yesterday when I was returning from Batam to Selat Panjang via Sekupang Port.

Upon arriving at the port, I went to the counter clearly marked "Dumai Line" to purchase a ticket. After paying and receiving my ticket, I was surprised to find that the ticket I was given actually said "Batam Jet."

I then asked the clerk, "Why Batam Jet? I want to take the Dumai Line."

The clerk didn't answer my question and simply said, "Big ship." I reiterated that I wanted a Dumai Line ticket, but the clerk remained silent. Then another clerk told me that the money couldn't be transferred back because the payment had already been made. Fortunately, my money was refunded in cash.

After that, I bought a ticket at the actual Dumai Line counter, which was right next to it, and got the correct ticket.

What made me even more upset was that my parents had experienced a similar experience. Because they weren't familiar with the writing, they only realized they hadn't purchased a Dumai Line ticket until they were about to board the ship and were told by the clerk.

I actually didn't intend to post this. However, because my parents also experienced the same incident, I feel the need to raise this complaint.

I ask the Sekupang Port Authority to follow up and monitor practices like this to prevent further confusion or harm to passengers, especially parents and passengers who may not understand the differences between ticket counters or the names of ship operators.

Hey guys, it’s your favorite elite traveler back with another unfiltered review—and this time, we need to talk about the gatekeeping situation at the Batam Center Ferry Terminal.

As an Indonesian who travels extensively, I am usually so proud to welcome international visitors to our beautiful country. But my recent arrival at Batam Center at 9:30 PM was, without exaggeration, an absolute NIGHTMARE. If this terminal is meant to be a major international gateway, the current reality is a total embarrassment to our national hospitality.

Here is the raw truth about what you can expect if you land here late at night:

1. The Immigration Bottle-Neck (The Absolute Worst Part)
Imagine an entire ferry of exhausted travelers arriving at 9:30 PM, only to find exactly one immigration officer working the counter. The inefficiency was mind-boggling.

But the real vibe-killer was the officer handling the desk—an older woman named Ibu May. To say she was rude is an understatement. Unprofessional, highly inefficient, and frankly, throwing what I can only describe as a 5-year-old’s tantrum behind the desk. As an Indonesian, it broke my heart to watch her. She is single-handedly ruining the image of Indonesian hospitality for every international tourist standing in that excruciatingly long line.

2. Zero Digital Readiness
Before you even get to the chaos inside, there is no coordination at the entrance. There are no QR codes shared or displayed at the entrance for required digital arrivals or health forms before you enter the terminal. Everyone is left scrambling in the dark, trying to figure out what they need to do. It’s clunky, outdated, and unacceptable for a major transit hub in 2026.

3. The Transport Monopoly Trap
Once you finally escape the terminal, don't even think about opening your Grab or Gojek apps. The terminal strictly bans ride-hailing apps to protect their local taxi monopoly.

Normally, I’m all for supporting local drivers, but the execution here is a safety and logistical hazard. Most of the drivers stationed there are very elderly, struggle to understand directions, and—unbelievably—do not know how to type into or use Google Maps to reach your destination. If you don't know the exact streets yourself, you are essentially stranded with a driver who can't navigate.

The Verdict 🚨
Batam Center Ferry Terminal needs a massive wake-up call, urgent staff retraining, and a complete tech overhaul. To the management: please address the lack of personnel, the attitude of staff like Ibu May, and let ride-hailing apps in so travelers can actually get home safely.

POSSIBLE ACT OF BRIBERY/ CORRUPTION

So last Friday (21/2/2025), three of us (mom, brother and me) was having our weekend trip to Batam.

We arrived at Batam Center Ferry Terminal at 9am local time. While lining up for passport check, I was setting up my roaming to fill up the Visa of Arrival (VOA). There, I was being called by an immigration lady to the office and both my mom’s and my phone, together with my passport was being taken by the immigration lady. Then, she told me to wait outside of her office (it was 9.30am Batam time). Roughly after 20-30 minutes, she went of of her office room to attend another offencer, but when she saw me, she asked me “kamu ngapain disini?” twice because I was super clueless. Then I told her that my phone and passport was taken by her. She then rudely told me “ha tahu pun kamu, kamu tahu nggak apa salahmu?” I replied, “aku tadi lagi setting my roaming service to fill my VOA”. Then, she told me that roaming can be done after immigration outside. I then just remained silent and nod softly. She then went back into her room and ghosted me for not sure how many hours. While waiting for her action, I was just sat on the chair, not provoking nor asking for a release because I believe she just did her job. Then, there was a man sat right to me asking what happened. I told him that my passport and phones were taken by the officer. He then softly told me that he can offer help. Me being suspicious with the offer (I can sense that his help came with a tipping/side money, I replied him “nggak papa. Aku tunggu aja”). This man then left me and went for another offender (not directly but periodically he will come into the room).

Bear in mind that throughout my wait, there were many offender after me that being released in less than 10 minutes waiting (one of them directly was with the guy who offered me help).

Fast forward, I was being held in the waiting area, from 9am until 1.30pm. When I was about to be released, the lady officer told me to not use phone anymore while waiting for the immigration check. Me being frustrated being held that long without phone and passport, replied her with a single word, “maybe”. She got furious and proceed to reject my entry. I told her that “that’s okay. Just send me back to Malaysia cause I was mentally and physically drained from the wait”.

While waiting for my return ferry, she came to me asking me to call my family. Apparently, when my ferry PIC informed my mom that I will be sent home for “rude” behaviour, my mum was asking the lady officer’s name from the ferry PIC, and wanted to report her for wrong accussation. I was being accused for playing my phone despite being warned twice by the other officer (in which, I was not being warned at all for the offense (if any). She then cleared my entry after hearing that my mom wanted to report her for possible act of corruption and misaccusation (because at 11.30am Batam time, my mom went into the waiting area to see me, and I told her that there was one local guy offered me for help). The last picture was the guy who offered me help, having a conversation with the lady officer.

This posting was not to accuse the officer for act of corruption, but for the visitor to be more aware of this frequent incidences of “random check/using phone while in immigration” offense. Also, for the public authority to investigate the presence of the guy offering me help in the Batam Center Ferry Immigration office. Why were he in the office most of the time. Also to Ms Cia, you owed me my 4 hours time waiting like a stupid guy, and you don’t deserve my respect.

CORRUPT IMMIGRATION OFFICERS AT THIS FERRY TERMINAL IMMIGRATION

On 21 February, my family and I made a plan to visit Batam, Indonesia. The Chinese New Year holiday had just passed, and we wanted a short, peaceful getaway—two days of rest and sightseeing before my mother returns to the Philippines. It was meant to be simple family time.

We are Philippine passport holders - husband, myself and my daughter have valid SG long term pass. Indonesians grant 30-day visa-free entry for Philippine passport holders. We had return tickets within the allowed period. We had hotel bookings. Everything was straightforward.

But the moment we reached immigration in Batam on 21 Feb 2026, 1030AM Indonesian time, things changed.

We were suddenly held back and questioned. The officers accused us of traveling to Batam “only to extend my mom’s visa in Singapore.” This accusation shocked us. Why would Indonesian immigration be concerned about Singapore’s ICA policies? We were entering Indonesia legally under Indonesia’s visa-free scheme. We were not overstaying anywhere. We were not violating any Indonesian law.

Despite explaining that this was a short 2-day leisure trip, we were escorted into an office for further “interrogation.”

The room was poorly lit and tense. There were other tourists inside as well, including an Indian passport holder who also appeared distressed. The atmosphere felt intimidating. Questions were repeated. The tone was accusatory, as if we had already done something wrong.

Then the officer’s tone changed.
He told us we had “two options”:
1. Change my mother’s flight and book her a ticket back to the Philippines on a date they wanted.
2. Pay SGD 150 as a “penalty” for “transiting” in Batam.

Penalty for what violation? There was no clear explanation. No written notice. No official receipt mentioned upfront. No formal charge. Just two “options.”

Why should Indonesian immigration dictate when my mother flies back to the Philippines? Why was there a “penalty” when we were within Indonesia’s visa-free entry rules?

At that moment, fear took over. We were in a foreign immigration office. We saw how the officer spoke to other tourists. We did not know what could happen next—would they deny entry? Cancel our passports? Blacklist us? Create further complications for our travel?

Feeling intimidated and powerless, and wanting to avoid further trouble, we agreed to pay the money.

What was supposed to be a relaxing family trip turned into a deeply stressful and unsettling experience. It leaves travelers questioning:
1. Are short leisure trips now suspicious?
2. Is visiting Batam after staying in Singapore automatically treated as wrongdoing?
3. Why are tourists pressured with vague “penalties” without clear written violations?

Experiences like this damage trust. Tourism thrives on safety, fairness, and transparency. When travelers feel intimidated or pressured without clear legal basis, it creates fear—not confidence.

We came for rest and sightseeing. We left with disappointment.

This will likely be our last visit to Batam.

To fellow travelers: always keep your documents complete, know your visa rules, and stay calm—but also be aware of your rights. No holiday should begin with fear.

I've passed through this terminal several times over the past year, so I've gotten pretty familiar with how it operates.
The Good:
The basics are covered well enough. There are plenty of SIM card kiosks right when you arrive, which is handy if you need to get connected immediately. Immigration processing is straightforward - nothing fancy, but it moves along at a reasonable pace. Luggage retrieval is simple and easy to navigate.
The real bonus is the overhead walkway that connects directly to Mega City Mall. Makes getting to the Grab taxi stand super convenient - you don't have to deal with touts or figure out where to go. Just walk across and you're there.
The Not-So-Good:
It's a functional terminal, but that's about it. Don't expect much in terms of amenities or comfort while you're waiting. The facility feels pretty basic and could use some updating to make the arrival/departure experience more pleasant.
Bottom Line:
Does the job for getting in and out of Batam, and the connection to Mega City Mall is genuinely useful for onward travel. It's not going to wow you, but it won't give you major headaches either. If you're a regular traveler to Batam like me, you'll appreciate the straightforward layout even if it's nothing special. Sonnet 4.5

⭐ 1/5 — Worst Travel Experience Ever.

Detained Without a Clear Reason.

I have travelled extensively across Europe, Turkey and Southeast Asia, and I can confidently say that this was the worst travel experience I have ever had.

My wife, our child and I travelled to Batam with friends for a simple weekend getaway. We cleared Malaysian Immigration, received our departure clearance and boarded the ferry without any issue.

The moment we arrived at the Batam ferry terminal, a police officer approached us, took our passports and brought our family into a room. Later, our child was allowed to leave with our friends while my wife and I were kept there.

We were made to wait for almost TWO HOURS with no proper explanation.

Only after we repeatedly demanded answers were we told that we were being detained because the Malaysian police had supposedly requested it.

That explanation made absolutely no sense.

If Malaysian authorities had actually placed any restriction on us, how did we clear Malaysian Immigration and legally depart Malaysia without any problem?

The whole situation ruined our trip. We no longer felt comfortable staying in Batam, so we choose to return to Malaysia immediately.

Here is the most shocking part.

When we arrived back in Malaysia, Malaysian Immigration interviewed us. We explained everything and asked what case or issue had caused us to be detained in Batam.

They could not identify any reason for it.

There appeared to be no case or immigration issue involving either of us. They were also puzzled as to why we had been detained after we had already cleared Malaysian Immigration normally.

So I would genuinely like to know:

Why were we detained for almost two hours?

Why were we separated from our child without a clear explanation?

Why were we told that Malaysian police had requested our detention when Malaysian authorities could not identify the reason for it?

Being detained in a foreign country without being clearly told why, especially while travelling with your child, is not something any traveller should have to experience.

What was supposed to be a relaxing weekend getaway turned into an extremely stressful and disturbing experience.

I am sharing this so other travellers are aware of what happened to us, and I sincerely hope the relevant authorities investigate and provide a proper explanation.

For us, this was completely unacceptable and easily the worst travel experience we have ever had.

⭐ 1/5 — Worst Travel Experience Ever.

Detained Without a Clear Reason.

I have travelled extensively across Europe, Turkey and Southeast Asia, and I can confidently say that this was the worst travel experience I have ever had.

My wife, our child and I travelled to Batam with friends for a simple weekend getaway. We cleared Malaysian Immigration, received our departure clearance and boarded the ferry without any issue.

The moment we arrived at the Batam ferry terminal, a police officer approached us, took our passports and brought our family into a room. Later, our child was allowed to leave with our friends while my wife and I were kept there.

We were made to wait for almost TWO HOURS with no proper explanation.

Only after we repeatedly demanded answers were we told that we were being detained because the Malaysian police had supposedly requested it.

That explanation made absolutely no sense.

If Malaysian authorities had actually placed any restriction on us, how did we clear Malaysian Immigration and legally depart Malaysia without any problem?

The whole situation ruined our trip. We no longer felt comfortable staying in Batam, so we choose to return to Malaysia immediately.

Here is the most shocking part.

When we arrived back in Malaysia, Malaysian Immigration interviewed us. We explained everything and asked what case or issue had caused us to be detained in Batam.

They could not identify any reason for it.

There appeared to be no case or immigration issue involving either of us. They were also puzzled as to why we had been detained after we had already cleared Malaysian Immigration normally.

So I would genuinely like to know:

Why were we detained for almost two hours?

Why were we separated from our child without a clear explanation?

Why were we told that Malaysian police had requested our detention when Malaysian authorities could not identify the reason for it?

Being detained in a foreign country without being clearly told why, especially while travelling with your child, is not something any traveller should have to experience.

What was supposed to be a relaxing weekend getaway turned into an extremely stressful and disturbing experience.

I am sharing this so other travellers are aware of what happened to us, and I sincerely hope the relevant authorities investigate and provide a proper explanation.

For us, this was completely unacceptable and easily the worst travel experience we have ever had.

POSSIBLE ACT OF BRIBERY/ CORRUPTION

So last Friday (21/2/2025), three of us (mom, brother and me) was having our weekend trip to Batam.

We arrived at Batam Center Ferry Terminal at 9am local time. While lining up for passport check, I was setting up my roaming to fill up the Visa of Arrival (VOA). There, I was being called by an immigration lady to the office and both my mom’s and my phone, together with my passport was being taken by the immigration lady. Then, she told me to wait outside of her office (it was 9.30am Batam time). Roughly after 20-30 minutes, she went of of her office room to attend another offencer, but when she saw me, she asked me “kamu ngapain disini?” twice because I was super clueless. Then I told her that my phone and passport was taken by her. She then rudely told me “ha tahu pun kamu, kamu tahu nggak apa salahmu?” I replied, “aku tadi lagi setting my roaming service to fill my VOA”. Then, she told me that roaming can be done after immigration outside. I then just remained silent and nod softly. She then went back into her room and ghosted me for not sure how many hours. While waiting for her action, I was just sat on the chair, not provoking nor asking for a release because I believe she just did her job. Then, there was a man sat right to me asking what happened. I told him that my passport and phones were taken by the officer. He then softly told me that he can offer help. Me being suspicious with the offer (I can sense that his help came with a tipping/side money, I replied him “nggak papa. Aku tunggu aja”). This man then left me and went for another offender (not directly but periodically he will come into the room).

Bear in mind that throughout my wait, there were many offender after me that being released in less than 10 minutes waiting (one of them directly was with the guy who offered me help).

Fast forward, I was being held in the waiting area, from 9am until 1.30pm. When I was about to be released, the lady officer told me to not use phone anymore while waiting for the immigration check. Me being frustrated being held that long without phone and passport, replied her with a single word, “maybe”. She got furious and proceed to reject my entry. I told her that “that’s okay. Just send me back to Malaysia cause I was mentally and physically drained from the wait”.

While waiting for my return ferry, she came to me asking me to call my family. Apparently, when my ferry PIC informed my mom that I will be sent home for “rude” behaviour, my mum was asking the lady officer’s name from the ferry PIC, and wanted to report her for wrong accussation. I was being accused for playing my phone despite being warned twice by the other officer (in which, I was not being warned at all for the offense (if any). She then cleared my entry after hearing that my mom wanted to report her for possible act of corruption and misaccusation (because at 11.30am Batam time, my mom went into the waiting area to see me, and I told her that there was one local guy offered me for help). The last picture was the guy who offered me help, having a conversation with the lady officer.

This posting was not to accuse the officer for act of corruption, but for the visitor to be more aware of this frequent incidences of “random check/using phone while in immigration” offense. Also, for the public authority to investigate the presence of the guy offering me help in the Batam Center Ferry Immigration office. Why were he in the office most of the time. Also to Ms Cia, you owned me my 4 hours time waiting like a stupid guy, and you don’t deserve my respect.

I was threatened with two options: pay immediately or be detained overnight and forced to return to Singapore the next day.

This was not enforcement. This was coercion and extortion targeting travellers.

CORRUPT IMMIGRATION OFFICERS AT THIS FERRY TERMINAL IMMIGRATION

On 21 February, my family and I made a plan to visit Batam, Indonesia. The Chinese New Year holiday had just passed, and we wanted a short, peaceful getaway—two days of rest and sightseeing before my mother returns to the Philippines. It was meant to be simple family time.

We are Philippine passport holders - husband, myself and my daughter have valid SG long term pass. Indonesians grant 30-day visa-free entry for Philippine passport holders. We had return tickets within the allowed period. We had hotel bookings. Everything was straightforward.

But the moment we reached immigration in Batam on 21 Feb 2026, 1030AM Indonesian time, things changed.

We were suddenly held back and questioned. The officers accused us of traveling to Batam “only to extend my mom’s visa in Singapore.” This accusation shocked us. Why would Indonesian immigration be concerned about Singapore’s ICA policies? We were entering Indonesia legally under Indonesia’s visa-free scheme. We were not overstaying anywhere. We were not violating any Indonesian law.

Despite explaining that this was a short 2-day leisure trip, we were escorted into an office for further “interrogation.”

The room was poorly lit and tense. There were other tourists inside as well, including an Indian passport holder who also appeared distressed. The atmosphere felt intimidating. Questions were repeated. The tone was accusatory, as if we had already done something wrong.

Then the officer’s tone changed.
He told us we had “two options”:
1. Change my mother’s flight and book her a ticket back to the Philippines on a date they wanted.
2. Pay SGD 150 as a “penalty” for “transiting” in Batam.

Penalty for what violation? There was no clear explanation. No written notice. No official receipt mentioned upfront. No formal charge. Just two “options.”

Why should Indonesian immigration dictate when my mother flies back to the Philippines? Why was there a “penalty” when we were within Indonesia’s visa-free entry rules?

At that moment, fear took over. We were in a foreign immigration office. We saw how the officer spoke to other tourists. We did not know what could happen next—would they deny entry? Cancel our passports? Blacklist us? Create further complications for our travel?

Feeling intimidated and powerless, and wanting to avoid further trouble, we agreed to pay the money.

What was supposed to be a relaxing family trip turned into a deeply stressful and unsettling experience. It leaves travelers questioning:
1. Are short leisure trips now suspicious?
2. Is visiting Batam after staying in Singapore automatically treated as wrongdoing?
3. Why are tourists pressured with vague “penalties” without clear written violations?

Experiences like this damage trust. Tourism thrives on safety, fairness, and transparency. When travelers feel intimidated or pressured without clear legal basis, it creates fear—not confidence.

We came for rest and sightseeing. We left with disappointment.

This will likely be our last visit to Batam.

To fellow travelers: always keep your documents complete, know your visa rules, and stay calm—but also be aware of your rights. No holiday should begin with fear.

Papan petunjuk arah tersedia dengan jelas, sehingga memudahkan pengunjung dalam mencari loket tiket, area imigrasi, dan ruang tunggu. Petugas di pelabuhan juga cukup sigap dalam membantu para penumpang, baik yang baru pertama kali datang maupun yang sudah sering bepergian.

Kebersihan di area pelabuhan juga terjaga dengan baik. Fasilitas umum seperti toilet, ruang tunggu, dan area makan cukup bersih dan nyaman. Selain itu, suasana di dalam pelabuhan cenderung tertib, dengan kontrol keamanan yang ketat tetapi tetap efisien. Proses imigrasi berjalan cukup cepat, terutama jika penumpang sudah menyiapkan dokumen yang dibutuhkan.

Dari segi aksesibilitas, Pelabuhan Batam Center terhubung langsung dengan pusat perbelanjaan, sehingga penumpang yang datang atau menunggu keberangkatan bisa berbelanja atau bersantap dengan nyaman. Tersedia pula berbagai moda transportasi, seperti taksi dan layanan transportasi online, yang memudahkan perjalanan ke berbagai wilayah di Batam. Secara keseluruhan, Pelabuhan Batam Center merupakan pelabuhan yang tertib, kondusif, dan memiliki fasilitas yang cukup baik. Bagi wisatawan maupun pelaku bisnis yang sering bepergian ke Singapura atau Malaysia, pelabuhan ini menjadi pilihan utama karena kepraktisan dan kenyamanan yang ditawarkannya.

Nongsapura Ferry Terminal in Batam, Indonesia, is a well-organized and efficient gateway for travelers heading to Singapore or other nearby islands. The terminal is relatively clean, with basic amenities such as waiting areas, snack stalls, and restrooms, though it could benefit from more seating and better maintenance. Immigration and boarding processes are generally smooth, but peak hours can see longer queues. The terminal’s location offers scenic waterfront views, adding a pleasant touch to the waiting experience. While not as modern as some international ferry hubs, Nongsapura serves its purpose effectively for short-distance travel. Improvements in signage and customer service could enhance the overall experience.
